Ideas to build for Search Desk

Each of these is already written up, so an agent can build it from its brief. Pick the one that would help Amira most, then ask for it by name. Small ones fit in one sitting. If none of them is right, describe your own.

Small about one sitting

Add to calendar Small

Put an interview or a starred event into your phone's calendar.

A date written in a tracker is easy to miss. In the calendar it gets a reminder.

Ask for it by name: calendar

AI: follow-up message Small

Drafts a short follow-up or thank-you note for a job. You copy it yourself.

Many people do not follow up because they do not know what to write. A short draft to edit removes the hard part.

Ask for it by name: recipe-followup

AI: sites for my field Small

Suggests job sites and organisations for your kind of work, as suggestions to add to sites.

Most people only know the big job sites. A good list for your trade or field is hard to find.

Ask for it by name: recipe-sites

Bigger text Small

Larger text and stronger contrast, remembered on this device.

Small grey text is hard to read for many people, on a phone or a library computer.

Ask for it by name: bigtext

Job sites Small

Keep the job sites you use in one place, with a note about each.

Job searching means many sites and it is easy to lose track of which ones you check. This also gives the AI's "new place to look" leads a home: you can take one, and it becomes a site.

Ask for it by name: sites

One-page summary Small

A page you can print or save as a PDF: this week's jobs, dates and events.

Some people do their search with paper, or bring a page to the library or a meeting with a worker. Other features can add their own section to this page.

Ask for it by name: print

Pay notes Small

The pay each posting gives, beside the pay you are aiming for.

Pay is easy to forget between postings. Seeing both numbers on a job helps you decide, and helps when an employer asks what you expect.

Ask for it by name: pay

Posting checklist Small

What a posting must tell you in Ontario, and whether this one does.

The 2026 posting rules say what a posting has to include. Checking each one takes a minute and shows which postings are careful with you.

Ask for it by name: checklist

Reply due Small

After an interview, shows the date the employer should have told you the result by.

In Ontario, employers have to tell you the outcome within a set time after the last interview (45 days in the 2026 rules). Knowing the date tells you when it is fair to ask.

Ask for it by name: reply-clock

This week Small

How many you applied to, followed up and went to this week. No streaks and no scores.

Job searching feels endless. A small plain count of what you did this week shows that you are moving, without pressure.

Ask for it by name: week

Which resume Small

Which version of your resume you sent where.

When an employer calls, you want to know which resume they have in front of them.

Ask for it by name: resumes

Medium a little longer

AI: weekly check-in Medium

Sends your open jobs and suggests the next step for each, as suggestions.

Once a week it helps to ask "what should I do next on each of these?" A free chat can give a short answer for each job, and you decide which to use.

Ask for it by name: recipe-weekly

My examples Medium

Short stories from your work, ready for interview questions; the coach recipe can include them.

Interviewers ask for examples ("Tell me about a time..."). It is much easier to answer when you wrote a few down in advance.

Ask for it by name: stories

People I met Medium

A short note about people you met, linked to an event or a job.

Most jobs come from people. A note about who you met, and what they said, is what you need when you write to them a week later.

Ask for it by name: contacts

None of these fits? Tell the agent what Amira struggles with, in your own words, and it will turn that into a plan.
